SMTO-CFG-0056 — A Gateway in SMTO's startup settings has no address

GUID: 208e9b8b-cf10-49b3-9a00-416585eac55b
Slug: config-gateway-url-must-be-non-empty-for
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • SMTO's startup settings name a Gateway — the helper program SMTO uses to run commands on a computer — but give it no address, so SMTO can't reach it and stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the person who set up SMTO's startup settings which Gateway entries they added, and find the one with an empty address. The startup settings, not the app's Settings page, hold the entry SMTO rejected.
  2. Enter that Gateway's address, for example http://127.0.0.1:8787 for a Gateway on the same computer as SMTO, or remove the entry. SMTO needs an address for every named Gateway before it can send commands there.
  3. Start SMTO again. To manage computers from the app instead, add them in Settings › Setup › Gateways once SMTO is running. Gateways added on that Settings page are stored separately and don't need a startup entry.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who installed SMTO. Don't enter the address of a different computer just to clear the error; commands would run on that computer instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Settings validation rejected the gateway_endpoints mapping because the URL for a named node is empty after trimming whitespace.

What this means

  • Gateway endpoint normalization produces an empty URL for a named node. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Gateway endpoint normalization produces an empty URL for a named node.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect that node's effective URL after trimming whitespace, keeping private transport material out of reports.

How to fix it

  • Find the gateway_endpoints entry for the node named in the message wherever Settings is constructed directly (Settings(...) or model_validate in embedding code or tests), set its Gateway URL (for a local Gateway typically http://127.0.0.1:8787) or remove the entry, then restart. get_settings does not populate gateway_endpoints, and a bad managed override (managed.json) is reported as the generic settings-schema 422 instead. Keep private connection details out of shared reports; this check does not test connectivity.
  • Configure the intended Gateway URL for the affected named node.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Each intended node has a nonempty supported endpoint address.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
